statement.p: (a) Find the point Q that is a distance 0.1 from the point P = (3, 2) in the direction of \mathbf{v} = \left\lt 3,-3\right>. Give five decimal places in your answer.
(b) Use P and Q to approximate the directional derivative of f(x,y) = \sqrt{x+y} at P, in the direction of \mathbf{v}.
(c) Give the exact value for the directional derivative you estimated in part (b).

static.solution:
(a) The unit vector \mathbf{u} in the same direction as \mathbf{v} is \mathbf{u} = \frac{1}{\Vert \mathbf{v}\Vert} \mathbf{v} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{18}} \mathbf{v} = \langle \frac{3}{\sqrt{18}}, \frac{-3}{\sqrt{18}} \rangle \approx \left\lt 0.707107,-0.707107\right>.
The vector \mathbf{w} of length 0.1 in the direction of \mathbf{v} is \vec w = 0.1\vec u = \left\lt 0.0707107,-0.0707107\right> The displacement vector from P to Q is \mathbf{w}. Hence Q = (3,2) + (0.0707107, -0.0707107) = (3.07071, 1.92929).
(b) Since the distance from P to Q is 0.1, the directional derivative of f at P in the direction of Q is approximately f_{u} \approx \frac{f(Q)-f(P)}{0.1} = \frac{2.23607 - 2.23607}{0.1} = 0.
(c) We have f_x = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+1y}}\quad\mbox{and}\quad f_y = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+1y}}, so \nabla f(3,2) = \left\lt 0.223607,0.223607\right>.
The directional derivative at P=(3, 2) in the direction of \mathbf{u} is f_u(3,2) = \nabla f(3,2)\cdot \mathbf{u} = 0.
